channel.title: OctoProbe News
channel.description: Investigative reporting on national security, intelligence, digital targeting and online influence operations, built from open-source records.

item.title: ‘Did Not Wish to Create Panic’: FOIA Records Rebuild the Official Story of the Kabul Evacuation
item.description: State Department OIG files released under FOIA rebuild the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal: a Kabul embassy that feared panic, bad evacuee counts, and Navy emails.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Three FOIA-released document excerpts on a navy card: State Department OIG report AUD-MERO-23-15, a Navy status report on 662 evacuees at Sigonella, and an August 27, 2021, email about 53 at-risk women stopped at a Taliban checkpoint

item.title: How to FOIA the Situation Room: One Request Pried Loose Thousands of Obama-Era Photos
item.description: A FOIA how-to built on a real win: case 24-09538-F freed 3,951 Obama Situation Room photos and 3,851 files. How to file, read exemptions and get copies.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Duotone photograph of President Obama in the Situation Room over a dark street map of Washington, with the words How to FOIA the Situation Room

item.title: Crowdfunding’s Hamas Problem: A Gaza Fundraiser’s Telegram Badge Leads to an Al-Qassam Chat
item.description: Two Chuffed pages raised $12,948 and $6,736 for a Gaza man whose Telegram status badge traces to a chat named for al-Qassam, Hamas’s armed wing.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Crowdfunding’s Hamas Problem: A Gaza Fundraiser’s Telegram Badge Leads to an Al-Qassam Chat

item.title: Subpoena, Order, Warrant: How the Government Gets Your Data
item.description: Two FOIA releases show how Congress, an inspector general and the courts compel records, and why a subpoena gets your subscriber data but not your messages.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Excerpts of a House subpoena, a Defense Department inspector general subpoena and a search warrant attachment above a three-step ladder: subpoena, 2703(d) order, warrant

item.title: Inside the FBI's CAST Guide: How Carriers and Agents Pin Down a Cell Phone
item.description: An FBI field guide shows how police make a phone reveal its location with silent texts, pings and tower timing, how precise it gets, and what the law requires.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Illustration: three cell towers on a stylized street grid, each casting a 120-degree sector and a range band that overlap around a red phone dot

item.title: Iran Says It Rules Hormuz. Its “Mine Strike” Stories Keep Falling Apart.
item.description: Iran’s Guards say a supertanker hit a mine near Hormuz on Oct. 20. No ship, no position, no outside confirmation, and a record of relabeled strikes.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Dark OctoProbe cover over a map of the Strait of Hormuz with a red pin at the narrows; at right, the yellow IRGC Navy title card reading Management of the Strait of Hormuz, beside the headline Iran Says It Rules Hormuz

item.title: How to FOIA an Official's Browser History, SharePoint Files and Teams Messages
item.description: A seven-step FOIA guide: find an agency's SharePoint with public DNS, name a custodian, and request browser logs, documents and Teams chats.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Street map of downtown Washington with a pin on Secret Service headquarters and the Secret Service star

item.title: DHS Lawyers Wrote 24 Pages on Buying Your Phone’s Location Data. They Withheld Every Page of the Analysis.
item.description: A DHS legal opinion on buying phone ad-ID location data came back under FOIA as one page and 23 withheld pages. How the trade works and what is still secret.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: DHS Lawyers Wrote 24 Pages on Buying Your Phone’s Location Data. They Withheld Every Page of the Analysis.

item.title: Jailed, Purged, Still Shipping: How ISIS Media Survives the Takedowns
item.description: A life sentence for its lead narrator and seized servers across Europe and North America have not stopped the weekly newspaper. Public records show the workarounds.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Dark OctoProbe cover over a map of Nigeria's Borno State and the Lake Chad basin; at right, the Islamic State weekly al-Naba masthead for issue 569 in white Arabic lettering with red diamonds, beside the headline Jailed, Purged, Still Shipping

item.title: CEFC, PLA Base 311, and the Long Gap from FBI Surveillance to Designation
item.description: FBI files show surveillance of a Confucius Institute from 2008; designation came in 2020. CEFC’s PLA Base 311 links were public in between. A dated timeline.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Cover: headline CEFC China Energy beside a tilted FBI file page dated December 1, 2008, over a dark map of Fuzhou with a red pin

item.title: North Korea's Fake IT Workers: Thin Covers, Borrowed Lives
item.description: We checked the eleven Gmail accounts DOJ tied to North Korean IT workers. Most had thin covers and new accounts. One rode what looks like a real American's history.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Cover: North Korean national flag over a dark map of Northeast Asia, with the headline Thin Covers, Borrowed Lives

item.title: The Only Public Map of CENTCOM’s War Orders Is Dated 2022
item.description: Op-ed: CENTCOM’s FOIA-released “Anvil Chart” shows how it stacks its war orders and what it hides. Iran-war modernization must start with authorities.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Op-ed cover: headline beside the U.S. Central Command emblem and a B-2 Spirit over a dark map of the Persian Gulf

item.title: Your Taxes, Their Target List: Following NED Money Into Ukraine’s Online Info-Ops Web
item.description: In 2016 NED paid Prometheus $100,000 for work on InformNapalm, a site that shares a mail server with Myrotvorets, a list naming Americans, and promotes it.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Your Taxes, Their Target List: OctoProbe cover over a map of Kyiv

item.title: 25 Pages of Press Clips: Leak Shows How Thin White House Vetting Really Was
item.description: Leaked transition files show White House vetting ran on 25-page clippings files, while the clearance system rewards speed and contracts over depth. Here is what real vetting pulls.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: 25 Pages of Press Clips: page one of the leaked Giuliani business-ties research file over a map of Washington

item.title: Alleged Saudi Spy List Leaked by Houthi-Tied Group, and Their Phones Do the Rest
item.description: Houthi-tied hackers dumped an alleged Saudi spy roster. Google Maps reviews tied to its contacts cluster in Riyadh, corroborating part of the leak.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: Alleged Saudi Spy List Leaked by Houthi-Tied Group: abstract identifier graph over Riyadh

item.title: Whose Coffee? An Anti-Bot Developer’s Handle Turns Up on Archive.today’s Donate Link
item.description: An anti-bot developer known as glizzykingdreko runs Takion API, a commercial bot-check bypass service. His donation page appeared in Archive.today’s donate link from August 2025 to October 2026. He now disclaims any tie. Here is the evidence chain, with confidence levels.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

item.title: Heather Zhang Case: OSINT Trail From a 2024 Reddit Allegation
item.description: Charged, not convicted: Irvine realtor Wanying "Heather" Zhang is accused of acting as an unregistered PRC agent. An OctoProbe investigation began from a January 2024 Reddit allegation naming Fatai Miao, whom CBS News identifies as "Individual 1." DOJ has not accused him of wrongdoing.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

item.title: Christopher W. Burns (FBI Most Wanted Fraudsters): Public Google Maps Activity Dated After His Last Sighting, Wayne, PA Area
item.description: A Google Maps account allegedly attributed to FBI Most Wanted Fraudster Christopher W. Burns shows activity in Wayne and Wynnewood, PA (~2021 and ~2023), after his last known sighting on September 24, 2020.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

item.title: From Public Lead to Identifier Graph
item.description: How OSINT teams turn one public clue into a sourced identifier graph—and how to avoid burning hours on manual markup or drowning in automated false-positive nodes.
item.dc:creator: Colin Aamot

media:content.media:description: From Public Lead to Identifier Graph
